newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin warns NATO over ex-Soviet republics.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin warns NATO over ex-Soviet republics.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin warned on Monday that any moves to bring former Soviet republics into NATO would "fully undermine" relations between Moscow and the Western defence alliance, Itar-Tass news agency said.

"I hope that through an open dialogue we will be able to convince those and other countries that their security will not increase by bringing them closer to NATO," Yeltsin said. "I do not even allow a thought that such a dialogue would fail. This would fully undermine relations between Russia and NATO."

Yeltsin is due to leave for Paris later on Monday to sign the Founding Act between Moscow and the Western defence alliance which addresses some of Russia's concerns over NATO's eastward expansion but does not prevent the enlargement.
Yeltsin reiterated his general opposition to NATO's expansion and said:

"The alternative is in creating a general and sweeping security system for the whole of Europe which will take into consideration security interests of every state, irrespective of its size, geographic position, economic or military potential."
